snapshot.content:
# Academic Record Progression Model

## Purpose

Academic Record should express progression, not just storage. This document defines the progression semantics that the page should represent so future UI and recommendation work uses the same mental model.

## Core Principle

A result is a historical event.
A progression signal is a derived interpretation of many results over time.

The Academic Record page must preserve that distinction.

## Progression Entities

### Attempt

A single submission or reviewed result event.

Minimum meaning:
- when the student did the work
- what assessment it belonged to
- which course, class, or module context applied
- what the scoring outcome was
- whether the result is final or still pending review

### Test

A reusable assessment identity that may have multiple attempts over time.

Why it matters:
- overview surfaces should often use the latest meaningful result per test
- progress should not be distorted by counting every retry as if it were a separate skill area

### Lens

A lens is an organizational view over the same results.

Approved lenses:
- course
- skill
- type
- THCS-specific progression
- writing-specific progression

A lens does not create new data. It reorganizes the same record set for interpretation.

## Derived Progression Levels

### 1. Raw History Level

Shows all attempts in chronological order.

Used for:
- auditability
- exact historical review
- result reopening

### 2. Latest-Meaningful-Result Level

Shows the latest relevant result per test or learning object.

Used for:
- overview cards
- recent-results surfaces
- simplified progress reading

### 3. Lens-Level Progression

Aggregates results by course, skill, or test type without inventing synthetic scores that hide the underlying record.

Used for:
- browsing the record
- spotting repeated weakness or strength areas
- future recommendation inputs

### 4. Track-Specific Progression

Specialized domains such as THCS and Writing can define their own progression surfaces when their internal logic is different enough that a generic lens is insufficient.

Used for:
- THCS-specific progress interpretation
- writing review and performance history

## Score Normalization Rules

The page may use simple shared metrics like percentage for lightweight summaries, but it must not pretend all scoring systems are identical.

Required guardrails:
- keep IELTS-native scoring semantics visible where relevant
- keep THCS-native scoring semantics visible where relevant
- treat percentage as a convenience metric, not the entire truth
- avoid single blended charts that imply full equivalence between IELTS and THCS performance

## Current Approved Progression Surfaces

### Overview Progression

Overview is allowed to summarize progression through:
- total tests
- average score
- best score
- recent results
- progressive feedback summary
- course, skill, and type lenses

### THCS Progression

THCS progression is allowed to remain specialized because the domain has its own expectations and reading patterns.

### Writing Progression

Writing progression is allowed to remain specialized because graded writing has pending-review states, teacher feedback, and different improvement rhythms from auto-marked tests.

## Progressive Feedback Role

Progressive feedback is a narrative interpretation layer on top of the result history.

It should:
- summarize recent momentum
- describe strengths and weaknesses in explainable language
- remain grounded in actual result evidence

It should not:
- replace raw result access
- become the only expression of progression
- hide uncertainty when the available data is thin

## Future Consumers Of Progression Data

The progression model is expected to support future systems such as:
- proficiency estimation
- material suggestions
- targeted skill recommendations
- intervention prompts for weak or declining areas
- teacher and student study prioritization

Those systems should consume stable derived metrics, not page-local UI state.

## Guardrails For Future Recommendation Work

Any future recommendation feature built on Academic Record should:
- cite the underlying learning lens it used
- distinguish recent weakness from long-term weakness
- respect pending-review and incomplete-result states
- avoid recommendations based on too little data
- remain auditable from the underlying result history

## Related Docs

- @doc/architecture/academic-record/academic-record-page-architecture
- @doc/architecture/academic-record/academic-record-analytics-readiness
- @doc/architecture/results-academic-record
- @doc/prd/prd-academic-record

- total tests
- average score
- best score
- recent results

Writing progression remains specialized because manual review, teacher feedback, and pending-review states behave differently from auto-graded history.

Course is currently expressed as a course-organized progression view over latest meaningful results.

- summarize recent momentum
